author: WP01
summary: The preface summarises what CNA is at the pin (C++23 XNA 4.0 reimplementation, independent platform/audio/renderer axes, 25 identities over 21 families), the sibling repositories, the evidence distinctions used throughout, and the C API status. Most facts are current and already on the site; the stated reason for the C API release-gate failure is stale at TARGET, and the book-structure and AI-production passages are book narrative. The not-a-game framing, sibling roles and evidence distinctions now live on the new foundations pages.

concepts.text: CNA's version API still reports 0.1.0-alpha.1 at the development snapshot; the snapshot is later than the only tag and has no new release name, and pre-1.0 a source-visible route is neither stable nor runtime-proven.

Platform integration, graphics and audio are independent build axes: SDL3 is the default platform and audio implementation while SDL2, headless, terminal, native X11, Wayland and Win32 platforms and NULL/ALSA audio exist under host gates.

target.evidence: cmake/PlatformSelection.cmake; audio selection CMake (via docs/platforms.html, Phase-1 verified)

concepts.text: 25 public renderer identities map to 21 implementation families; a multi-renderer build chooses one renderer at run time before its first graphics device is created.
CNA is neither a game nor an editor-centred engine but a compatibility framework for native C++ programs written in the shape of Microsoft::Xna::Framework.

Adjacent repositories provide what CNA should not duplicate: sharp-runtime (.NET-shaped types), easy-gl and meta-gl (the GL layer of five identities), free-direct and free-api (a narrow legacy route), xna4-spec (searchable API surface), and the sample and example repositories (user-level exercise).

Source inspection, a build, an execution, a renderer trace, an independent oracle and a pixel comparison establish different things, and bugs, partial routes and unsupported configurations stay visible because they affect engineering decisions.

target.evidence: methodology; applied on the new page

concepts.text: The work describes itself as both a technical monograph and a reference, and warns that it is not live API documentation but a revision-bounded map to be checked against the current repository.
concepts.note: Book self-description; the site states its own pin on every page (evidence box, doc-meta line).

concepts.text: The experimental native C API is at ABI 0.29.0 and its version is independent of the CNA product version; neither number substitutes for the source pin, and the alpha.1 renderer-map compile blocker is historical.
The preface attributes the failing C API release gate to three newly present modules not yet classified by the coverage-scope model.
concepts.note: At TARGET the gate fails on 468 unmapped public symbols, not on unclassified modules; the site's C API page already states the TARGET reason.

target.evidence: docs/c-api/RELEASE_GATE.md at 009d40f5: 'Not ready', the one unmet criterion is 'No public C++ symbol is unaccounted for' with 468 public symbols unmapped

concepts.text: The book's organisation follows the path of a call through the system, part by part, from ecosystem and framework to graphics, renderers, content, services, platforms and verification.
concepts.note: Book structure; the site is organised as a knowledge graph (docs, Development, Deep Dives), not by book parts.

concepts.text: API presence, successful compilation, execution, renderer engagement, behavioural comparison and pixel comparison are different observations; a green result is reported at the narrowest level the evidence supports, which separates a working path from a source-visible implementation, a historical run or a test that skipped.
The production process used AI-agent assistance, with authority for technical claims resting on identified source and evidence rather than on the drafting tool.
